description: Uncover a lost royal shrine, a rebellious abbey gate and one of Britain's tiniest pubs.
short_description: Chase a vanished king through abbey ruins before squeezing into a famously tiny pub.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 10+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A compact central route. Abbey Gardens opening times vary, but its main historical area is normally free to enter.

before_you_go.terrain: A compact central route using public pavements and public-garden paths whose opening times can vary.
before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.
before_you_go.accessibility: Public pavements and paths throughout; check current diversions if step-free access is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check local public facilities before setting off; customer toilets may depend on opening hours.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable walking shoes should be suitable.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the finishing venue’s current dog policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally possible on public paths; check temporary diversions and busy crossings.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Enter through the gate rebuilt after a town rose against an abbey.
stops.Hint_1: Start on Angel Hill, facing the formal Abbey Gardens.
stops.Hint_2: Find the enormous stone gateway with a single central arch.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Abbey Gate was rebuilt in the 14th century after townspeople damaged the earlier gateway during the riots of 1327. It once controlled the grand secular entrance to one of medieval England's richest abbeys.

stops.Stop_Name: Abbey Ruins and St Edmund's Shrine
stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find the broken stone heart of a mighty monastery built around a murdered king.
stops.Hint_1: Walk east through Abbey Gardens among the ruins.
stops.Hint_2: Head towards the modern marker for the shrine of St Edmund.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The abbey grew around the shrine of St Edmund, the East Anglian king killed by Vikings in 869. Pilgrims made it one of England's richest Benedictine monasteries before Henry VIII's dissolution closed it in 1539.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a square Norman giant that has guarded an absent abbey church for nine centuries.
stops.Hint_1: Return west towards the cathedral side of the gardens.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the massive stone tower standing separately beside St Edmundsbury Cathedral.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Built between about 1120 and 1148, the Norman Tower was the principal gateway into the abbey church. The church beyond it vanished after the Dissolution, but this remarkably complete Romanesque gateway survived and now serves as the bell tower for St Edmundsbury Cathedral.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Seek a flint-faced survivor that has been a house, tavern, prison and museum.
stops.Hint_1: Head north-west towards Cornhill and the market.
stops.Hint_2: Find the ancient stone building with arched windows at the south end of Cornhill.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Moyse's Hall dates from around 1180. Across its long life it has served as a townhouse, tavern, workhouse, police station and prison; it became a museum in 1899. Its collections now tell stories of local life, crime and witchcraft.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Your last kingdom is only fifteen feet long and seven feet wide. Squeeze in if you can.
stops.Hint_1: Walk south from the market into The Traverse.
stops.Hint_2: Find the tiny pub front at number 17, named The Nutshell.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The Nutshell measures roughly 15 feet by 7 feet and is celebrated as one of Britain's smallest pubs. Its walls and ceiling are packed with curios, including old banknotes and a reputedly mummified cat. End your royal pilgrimage with a drink in a truly tiny finale.
